Throughout 2024 the OECD was invited to share insights from the Competitiveness Outlook assessment and contribute to discussions on key thematic issues particularly within the Western Balkans region. This involvement included exchanging good practices for specific policy implementations and learning from ongoing developments beyond the assessments findings. By engaging with regional stakeholders and institutions the OECD was able to disseminate best practices and emerging trends identified through its assessment further supporting collaborative efforts to strengthen economic and digital competitiveness across the region.Center for Research and Policy Making CRPM 2829 May 2024 The OECD was invited to participate in a conference titled The Undeclared Political Economic and Sustainable Future of the Western Balkans held in Skopje North Macedonia. Commemorating CRPMs 20th anniversary this regional event featured four panels with the OECD serving as a panelist in the third discussion on Shaping the Economy of Tomorrow Assessing the Viability of Social Educational and Health Systems within the Current Economic Framework and the Aspirations of Generation Z. Additionally the conference included workshops on digitalisation economic cooperation between Poland and North Macedonia climate change and security and the establishment of circular supply chains.Regional Cooperation Council RCC 810 July 2024 The OECD attended the second HighLevel Cybersecurity Conference titled Cybersecurity Challenges and Opportunities in the Western Balkans organised by the Regional Cooperation Council RCC and held in Tirana. The conference featured four panels focusing on cybersecurity priorities in the region critical infrastructure the European Cybersecurity Certification Framework and the role of emerging technologies. This event provided an excellent opportunity to gain insights into the latest developments relevant EU policies and best practices in cybersecurity which are particularly pertinent to the OECDs work under the Competitiveness Outlook assessment subdimension 4.3 and to strengthen collaboration between the OECD and the RCC. Increasing Albanias Footprint in the Regional Digital Economy Sector Conference 2 October The OECD participated in the Increasing Albanias Footprint in the Regional Digital Economy Sector conference coorganised by the Foreign Investors Association and the Ministry of Economy Culture and Innovation of Albania. The OECD had a speaking role in Panel 1 Digitalisation and Value Creation for a Countrys Economy alongside representatives from DG NEAR the Swedish government and regional Tech Centers. The conference brought together key Albanian public institutions and local and international businesses focused on technology as their core activity.COP 29 Cross Regional Dialogue on Investing for Gender Equality 1718 October 2024 The OECD was invited to attend the COP 29 Cross Regional Dialogue on Investing for Gender Equality and Inclusive Action conference organized by the GRC Istanbul Center in collaboration with the UNDP on 1718 October 2024. At the event the OECD presented the genderspecific findings from the OECD Western Balkan Competitiveness Outlook 2024 and supported the participation of two representatives from the Western Balkans. This engagement further contributed to the dialogue on gender equality and inclusive action in the region.

description.narrative: A13: Support the establishment of the CE platforms

comment.narrative: The OECD adopted multiple measures for the establishment of CE platforms in all Western Balkan economies while promoting regional exchange and cooperation in this field. These include the nomination of six CE coordinators and the creation of six CE platforms in each of the WB economies as well as one regional platform the Regional Circular Economy Peer Dialogue. In the case of Albania and North Macedonia the two economies that had not yet commenced the development of a CE roadmap at the time the project started the newly nominated coordinators were instructed to form a CE stakeholder platformworking group to steer the process. In the remaining economies the OECD engaged with already existing CE platforms to exchange and foster collaboration within the scope of the project.The Regional CE Peer Dialogue platform was established in April 2023 in Istanbul during the regional launch meeting of the Supporting Green Transition through Circular Economy Roadmaps project. Endorsed by all the participants the platforms aim is to facilitate bi and multilateral exchange peerlearning and policy dialogue on how to design implement and monitor progress in circular economy transition efforts in the Western Balkans and beyond. In addition to the WB6 representatives from the OECD member state are also active members of the platform sharing their knowledge and good practices including in the development of the CE roadmaps of Albania and North Macedonia.

title.narrative: A14: Identification of CErelated needs

description.narrative: A14: Identification of CErelated needs

comment.narrative: To identify the circular economyrelated needs i.e. the forms of support that the economies would need to successfully design and implement their circular economy roadmaps the OECD held six rounds of virtual meetings with the CE contact points from all Western Balkans economies including the newly appointed coordinators of Albania and North Macedonia. CErelated needs identified varied as economies were at different stages of developing their CE roadmaps. Albania and North Macedonia required design support as they had not started the development of a CE roadmap by that time. The need for implementation support was voiced primarily by the economies with advanced CE roadmaps such as Montenegro and Serbia that have already adopted national strategies or Bosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo that were in the process of developing CE roadmaps at the time the OECD approached them.A regional Kickoff Meeting to kickstart the project Supporting Green Transition through Circular Economy Roadmaps was held at the OECD Istanbul Centre on the 19 April 2023 gathering more than 50 participants policy makers and practitioners from the Western Balkans selected OECD member states the OECD and the European Commission. The event also had a thematic focus policy discussion on plastic pollution complemented with an onsite visit thus representing the first regional peer learning event.

title.narrative: A15: Support design of the circular economy roadmaps

description.narrative: A15: Support design of the circular economy roadmaps

comment.narrative: The OECD developed the CE roadmaps in Albania and North Macedonia which were launched in March 2024. Both roadmaps were developed through a multistep process engaging diverse stakeholders from the government private sector civil society academia and the international community in an ongoing dialogue coordinated by the government Ministry of Tourism and Environment of Albania and Ministry of Economy of North Macedonia. The development of the roadmap started with a comprehensive diagnostic of key economic and environmental factors identifying gaps in both policy and practice. Based on its results and a tailored OECD prioritisation methodology key priority areas for the circular economy transition in Albania and North Macedonia were determined. This encompassed qualitative and quantitative analyses coupled with stakeholder discussions which informed the choice of the final priority areas. The CE roadmap of Albania unveils 35 policy recommendations across three priority areas where circular economy policies can have a significant impact in Albania economic instruments circular business models for SMEs and targeted solutions for plastics with a focus on marine litter. The CE roadmap of North Macedonia entails 41 policy recommendations across five priority areas circular business models for SMEs construction biomass and food textile industry and mining and metallurgy.These recommendations supported by a monitoring framework should serve as a cornerstone for propelling Albania and North Macedonia towards a more sustainable and circular future.

title.narrative: A16: Support for implementation of economyspecific roadmaps

description.narrative: A16: Support for implementation of economyspecific roadmaps

comment.narrative: Support for implementation is being carried out in a dynamic process. The Regional Kickoff event and policy exchange on the topic Combatting Plastic Pollution in Istanbul in April 2023 served as the first support for implementation activity. The event revolved around policy discussions supported by the findings of the OECD Global Plastics Outlook report. Hungary Italy and Trkiye provided inspiration by sharing lessons learnt and real examples on acting against plastic pollution and advancing circular economy. The meeting preceded an onsite visit to the Elif Packaging solutions production plant in Istanbul an opportunity to discover how discussed plastic combatting policies and solutions are put into effect and to experience how a circular business model works in practice.Circular economy roadmap launch events in Albania and North Macedonia held in March 2024 supported the implementation of circular economy roadmaps in respective economies through panel discussions titled From Design to Implementation. These discussions highlighted critical support factors and common pitfalls to avoid in implementing CE measures. The panels drew on insights from countries within the Regional CE Peer Dialogue Platform Italy Slovenia Montenegro Serbia that have advanced in the circular economy transition or have extensive experience in this area.In April 2024 support for implementation activities were organised as part of the World Circular Economy Forum 2024 in Brussels. In addition to participating in the Forumwhich provided Western Balkans peers with the latest insights into circular economy CE and fostered CE implementationthe OECD South East Europe Regional Programme and the European Commission DirectorateGeneral for Neighbourhood and Enlargement Negotiations DG NEAR organised a Joint Accelerator session on 18 April 2024 titled Driving the Circular Economy Transition with Private Sector Initiatives. The session emphasised the pivotal role of businesses in implementing the EUs Circular Economy Action Plan and propelling the circular transition in the EU Neighbourhoods the Western Balkans the Eastern Partnership and the Southern Neighbourhood. Businesses and entrepreneurs from Egypt Georgia Jordan and North Macedonia presented their innovative approaches to circularity demonstrating efforts to create jobs develop circular products and preserve natural capital and biodiversity amid rising material consumption.
